content.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll explore the workspace and set up a small book-tracking app with JSON file persistence.

text: Starting from scratch. Checking the root directory for any existing files.
Adding a GET endpoint for book detail pages and a POST endpoint to mark books as finished.

content.text: Building a simple Express app with JSON file storage and server-rendered pages for shareable book links.

args.command:
cd /workspace && node server.js &
sleep 1
# Test home page
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3000/
echo " GET /"

# Add a book
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://localhost:3000/books \
  -d "title=The%20Left%20Hand%20of%20Darkness&author=Ursula%20K.%20Le%20Guin&notes=A%20masterpiece%20of%20speculative%20fiction."
echo " POST /books"

# Read books.json
cat /workspace/data/books.json

# Get book ID and test detail page
BOOK_ID=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/workspace/data/books.json','utf8'))[0].id)")
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:3000/books/$BOOK_ID"
echo " GET /books/:id"

# Mark finished
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "http://localhost:3000/books/$BOOK_ID/finish"
echo " POST /books/:id/finish"

# Verify status
node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/workspace/data/books.json','utf8'))[0].status)"

# Test 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3000/books/nonexistent
echo " GET /books/nonexistent"

kill %1 2>/dev/null || true

content.text:
Your reading list app is ready. Here's what it does:

**Home (`/`)** — Add a book (title, author, optional notes), see what you're currently reading, and browse finished books. Each in-progress book has a "Mark finished" button.

**Book detail (`/books/:id`)** — Shows title, author, and notes. This URL is shareable — anyone with the link can view that book. You can also mark it finished from here.

**Storage** — Books are saved to `data/books.json`, so they persist across restarts.

Run it with:

```bash
npm start
```

Then open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). For auto-restart on file changes:

```bash
npm run dev
```
